title: Model Dimensionality (Integer, Textable, Numeric)
description: Dimensionality of a machine learning model (e.g., embedding vector size)
documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a single integer that describes the output dimensionality of a model, most commonly the size of its embedding vectors. This allows caps to advertise or negotiate the dimension of their output without needing a full model-info record.

## When to use
Use this type as a lightweight parameter or output when only the vector dimension is needed — for example, to size a vector database index or validate that an embedding model's output matches a downstream consumer's expected dimension.

## Notes
The minimum value is 1. Typical embedding models produce dimensions between 128 and 4096. The value should match the `embedding_dim` field in [LLM Model Info](https://capdag.com/browse/media:llm-model-info;json;record) or the `embedding_dim` field in [Embedding Vector](https://capdag.com/browse/media:embedding-vector;textable;record) for the same model.

## Number kind
Refines a numeric value with its number-system domain. A numeric value without a
number-kind tag is unconstrained on this axis. Adding a kind narrows what arithmetic
and comparison operations are well-defined on the value.

A whole number, positive, negative, or zero. No fractional part. Suitable for counts,
indices, ranks, and any quantity that cannot meaningfully take a decimal value.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
